. This is an Appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, "L.A.Act")
preferred by the Acquiring Body against the Judgment and Award dated 02.01.2012 passed by the learned Joint Civil Judge (Senior Division), Yavatmal (for short, 'Reference Court') in Land Acquisition Case No.143/2005 awarding the compensation @ Rs.1,50,000/- per hectare for the Claimants' acquired land admeasuring 11 H. 22 R., situated at mouza Bhatmarg, Tq. Babhulgaon,
District Yavatmal.
The cross- objection is filed by the Claimants for double enhancement in the compensation on the ground that, the acquiring land was irrigated land.
2. The above referred land of the Claimants was acquired for submergence of Bembla River Project.
The Section 4 Notification was issued on 17.12.1998.
The Land Acquisition Officer (L.A.O.) declared the Award on 19.06.2001 and determined the compensation @ Rs.58,324/- per hectare and Rs.39,070/- for well.
The Claimants filed the reference under Section 18 of the L.A.Act before the learned Reference Court.

The learned Reference Court enhanced the compensation @ Rs.1,50,000/-
per hectare and Rs.50,000/- towards the well.
3. Heard the learned Advocate for the Acquiring Body and the learned Advocate for the Claimants.

sentences.text: The learned Advocate for the Acquiring Body fairly submitted that, the compensation enhanced by the learned Reference Court was within four (4) times of the rate determined by the Special Land Acquisition Officer (S.L.A.O.).

The Government of Maharashtra had taken policy decision and issued the Government Resolution not to prefer the Appeals where the enhanced compensation is within four (4) times of the compensation determined by the S.L.A.O.
He submitted that, the cross-objection for further enhancement needs no consideration.

He submitted that, even considering the Claimants' land as irrigated land, this Court in First Appeal No.145/2024 decided on 23.01.2024 enhanced the compensation @ Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare for irrigated land which was acquired for the same project.

In support of his submissions, he relied on the decision in the State of Maharashtra Vs. Prashram Jagannath Aute, 2007(5) Mh.L.J. 403, wherein it is observed that, the Court has to determine the amount of compensation/market value of the land at the date of publication of the notification and on the facts and circumstances of each case and it was neither permissible nor proper to lay down any strait- jacket formula universally applicable to all land acquisition cases at any level of proceedings.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra Vs. Prashram Jagannath Aute, 2007(5) Mh.L.J. 403

He further relied on the decision in the Executive Engineer, Minor Irrigation Works, Jalgaon Vs. Vitthal Damodar Patil and Anr., (2019) 7 SCC 225,
wherein it is observed that, every reference proceeding must be decided on the basis of the evidence produced and the issues raised by the parties in the proceedings.

entities.text: Executive Engineer, Minor Irrigation Works, Jalgaon Vs. Vitthal Damodar Patil and Anr., (2019) 7 SCC 225
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: b] It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Claimants that, the S.L.A.O. granted the compensation for well in addition to compensation for land and the learned Reference Court enhanced the compensation for well, which goes to show that, the Claimants' land was irrigated land.

As the learned Reference Court determined the rate of Rs.1,50,000/- considering the land as dry land, the Claimants were entitled for double compensation @ Rs.3,00,000/- per hectare as there was well in the acquired land.

In support of his submission, he relied on the decision in Chindha Fakira Patil (Dead) Through LRs. Vs. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Jalgaon, (2011) 10 SCC 787, wherein it was observed that, "when it was not in dispute that there were wells in the acquired land, the mere fact that the appellants had not cultivated sugarcane or wheat cannot lead to an inference that the land was not irrigated .....".

entities.text: Chindha Fakira Patil (Dead) Through LRs. Vs. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Jalgaon, (2011) 10 SCC 787

double market rate of jirayat land has to be awarded for the irrigated land.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra and Anr. Vs. Baliram Girdhar Patil, 2006 (6) Mh.L.J. 82

He further relied on the decision in Prakash s/o. Anandrao Raut (Dead) through LRs. Vs. The State of Maharashtra and Ors.
of this Court in First Appeal No.1166/2008 decided on 22.12.2025, wherein double rate was enhanced than the rate determined for the dry crop land.
4.

sentences.text: As regards the Appeal of the Acquiring Body is concerned, it is covered by the Government Resolution Dated 03.11.2016 and Corrigendum dated 23.02.2017.

As the enhanced rate of Rs.1,50,000/- per hectare by the Reference Court is within four times of the rate determined by the L.A.O. @ Rs.58,324/- per hectare, the Appeal of the Acquiring Body needs no further consideration.
5. There cannot be any dispute in respect of the observations in the above referred Judgments cited by both the sides.
There is no dispute in respect of the extent of land of the Claimants acquired for submergence in the Bembla project.
In the reference applicable, it is stated by the Claimants that,
the acquired land was the irrigated land and the irrigation facility was available from well.

In the cross-objection of the Claimants, it has come that, he used to take the crop of tur, cotton, which were Vidarbha Irrigation Development ... vs Hansaraj S/O Dayalal Bhansari And 3 ... on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144969643/

sentences.text: The learned Reference Court enhanced the compensation @ Rs. 1,50,000/- per hectare.

6. The above referred First Appeal No. 145/2024 decided by the Judgment dated 23.01.2024, shows that, the said Appeal was in respect of acquisition for the Bembla project out of the same Section 4 Notification dated 17.12.1998 and award dated 19.06.2001.

This Court on the basis of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and earlier decision of this Court in respect of acquisition for the same project, enhanced the compensation @ Rs.1,20,000/- per hectare for dry crop land and @
Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare for irrigated land.

The relevant observations from the said Judgment is reproduced below :
"4. Learned advocate for the appellant submitted that this appeal would be covered by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal Nos. 7860-61 of 2023 (Arvind Madhaorao Patil and others vs. State of Maharashtra and others),
decided on 28.11.2023, in respect of another land of the appellant bearing survey No.
42.

entities.text: Arvind Madhaorao Patil and others vs. State of Maharashtra and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate submitted that the land bearing survey no.63, which is the subject matter of this appeal and the land bearing survey No. 42, which is the subject matter of the appeal before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, were owned by the appellant.
Both lands were similarly situated.
Learned advocate pointed out that the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation @ Rs.1,20,000/- per hectare in respect of dry crop land.
As far as irrigated land is concerned

, learned advocate relied upon the decision rendered by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in First Appeal No. 829 of 2013 (Bhaskar Mehetre vs. State of Maharashtra and others), decided on 24.01.2018 and submitted that in the case of the irrigated part of land bearing survey No. 61, the compensation was awarded @ Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare.

entities.text: First Appeal No. 829 of 2013 (Bhaskar Mehetre vs. State of Maharashtra and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate pointed out that in this case, the Reference Court recorded a finding that the land admeasuring 7.13 HR was dry crop land and the land admeasuring 4.04 HR was irrigated land.

Learned advocate submitted that the appellant is entitled to get compensation @ Rs.1,20,000/- per hectare in respect of dry crop land and @
Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare for irrigated land."
7.

The decision dated 24.01.2018 in First Appeal No.829/2013 (Bhaskar Mehetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.) of this Court referred in the above referred decision dated 23.01.2024 shows that, it was the Appeal wherein the land from the same village Bhatmarg was acquired from the same project i.e. Bembla Project under the same Award dated 16.06.2001.

entities.text: First Appeal No.829/2013 (Bhaskar Mehetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court, in the said Judgment by referring to the earlier Judgments enhanced the rate @ Rs.1,20,000/- per hectare for dry land and @ Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare for the irrigated land.
The relevant observations from the said Judgment are reproduced below :
"3. Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant filed reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which was numbered as Land Acquisition Case No.553 of 2003.

By the impugned judgment and order dated 19-04-2006, the reference Court increased the compensation and directed that it shall now be paid to the appellant at the rate of Rs.1,48,000/- per hectare for 4 hectares and 8 acres for the acquired land Vidarbha Irrigation Development ... vs Hansaraj S/O Dayalal Bhansari And 3 ... on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144969643/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and an amount of Rs.5,51,696/- for the Orange trees as also an amount of Rs.1,74,330/- for the well located on the land.
It appears that for the remaining 2 hectares of land, separate compensation was not given by the reference Court.
4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and order of the reference Court, the present appeal has been filed.

During the pendency of this appeal, by judgment and order dated 05-02-2016 passed in First Appeal No.632 of 2013, arising out of land acquisition proceedings pertaining to the same notification under Section 4 of the aforesaid Act and in pursuance of the very same award dated 16-06-2001, this Court held that the claimants were entitled to compensation at the rate of Rs.1,20,000/- per hectare for dry crop land and Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare for irrigated land.

The aforesaid judgment and order of this Court has been followed in a recent judgment and order dated 18-01- 2018 passed in First Appeal No.890 of 2016 pertaining to the acquisition of land in pursuance of the very same Notification under Section 4 of the aforesaid Act for the said village.
5. Therefore, on the principle of parity, the appellant/claimant in present appeal also deserves enhanced compensation.

Since, it is found that out of total area of land of the appellant that was acquired 4 hectares and 8 acres of land was irrigated land, I hold that the appellant is entitled to compensation at the rate of Rs. 1,80,000/- per hectare for the said acquired area of land.
Insofar as the balance 2 hectares of land is concerned, treating the same as dry crop land, I hold that the appellant shall be entitled to compensation at the rate of Rs. 1,20,000/- per hectare

As regards the compensation for Orange trees is concerned, although the appellant has sought further enhanced compensation, perusal of the valuation report dated 18- 04-1999 (Exhibit 59) and the evidence of the expert, shows that there is no material on record to support the contention of the appellant that he is entitled for further enhanced compensation for the Orange trees.

6. In the light of above, the impugned judgment and order of the reference Court is modified to the extent that for 4 hectares and 8 acres of the acquired land the appellant shall be entitled for compensation of Rs 1,80,000/- per hectare and for the balance 2 hectares of land the appellant shall be entitled to compensation of Rs.
1,20,000/- per hectare.
Needless to say that the appellant shall be entitled to statutory benefits on the enhanced compensation."

8. The above decision goes to show that, this Court has enhanced the compensation to the similarly placed Claimants, whose lands were acquired for the very same project @ Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare for the irrigated land.

True it is that, double the rate of the dry crop land is to be granted for the perennially irrigated land, however, once this Court in near about 4 cases i.e. the 2 referred above and the 2 mentioned in the above referred Judgment dated 24.01.2018 in First Appeal No.829/2013 has considered and enhanced the rate for irrigated land @ Rs.1,80,000/-, the same rate will have to be granted to the Claimants on the ground of parity.
Thus, the cross-objection succeeds to that extent.

Hence, the following order :
Vidarbha Irrigation Development ... vs Hansaraj S/O Dayalal Bhansari And 3 ... on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144969643/

sentences.text: i] The Appeal preferred by the Acquiring Body stands dismissed in view of the above referred Government Resolution and the Corrigendum.

ii] The Claimants are held entitled for enhanced compensation @ Rs.1,80,000/- per hectare for the acquired land admeasuring 11 H. 22 R. situated at village Bhatmarg, Tq. Babhulgaon,
District Yavatmal.
iii] The statutory benefits be calculated on the enhanced amount of compensation.

iv] The amount of compensation deposited by the Acquiring Body under the Award,
is allowed to be withdrawn by the Claimants, if not withdrawn earlier.
v] The Acquiring Body is expected to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation in the office of this Court within a period of four (4) months.
vi] The Appellant shall pay the Court fees on the enhanced amount of compensation as per Rules before withdrawal of compensation amout.
vii] Record and proceedings be sent back to the learned Tribunal.
